question: How many terms are in the arithmetic sequence \(13,\) \(16,\) \(19,\) \(\dotsc,\) \(70,\) \(73?\)
solution:
Consecutive terms differ by \(3\), so count how many \(3\)-unit steps take us from \(13\) to \(73\). The total increase is \(73-13=60\), giving
\[
\frac{60}{3}=20
\]
gaps. There is one starting term, and each gap leads to one additional term. Therefore the sequence has \(20+1=\boxed{21}\) terms, choice B.
